evidence_class: Mocked Redis (fakeredis WATCH transactions) and a fake clock; empty fixture cluster; no Kubernetes, node autoscaler or provider call was made.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.admission.PendingAdmission.admit, activate, release, held, pending and pending_execution_admission_total
Policy: global pending cap, per swarm pending cap, reservation lifetime, approved templates and a default request profile
Decision outcomes admitted, replayed, deferred and impossible; counters record admitted, deferred, impossible, expired, activated and released, never replays

scripts.swarm.tick._spawn admits each task inside the spawn loop after the capacity checks when the runtime carries an admission: impossible tasks are blocked on the ledger with the reason, deferred tasks wait, a refused claim, a ledger refusal or a failed spawn releases the reservation, the spawned task carries its reservation
scripts.swarm.tick._launch_checks activates the task reservation when the launch check passes, ending its pending state

supported_versions.redis: WATCH, MULTI, sorted sets and hashes; no Lua and no server clock
supported_versions.compatibility: A runtime without an admission attribute spawns exactly as before; the local herdr path is unchanged

authority: Admission runs inside the swarm tick and takes the swarm slug from its caller; it performs no grant check of its own. Caps come only from the Policy the runtime constructs; no task field, display label or provider name widens a cap. A grant check belongs to the runtime that constructs PendingAdmission.

states.observed: Cases A, B and C each passed twice from independent fake Redis state. Focused admission, tick, launch check and size limit tests passed.
states.accepted: From zero remote capacity three of ten runnable tasks hold pending reservations, six are deferred in order, the impossible memory request is rejected and holds nothing.
states.committed: Code and fixture inputs are at tested_commit.
states.externally_verified: None: no Kubernetes runtime adapter carries an admission yet, and no live G3 deployment was exercised.

validation.command: python -m pytest tests/test_swarm_v2_admission.py tests/swarm/test_tick.py tests/swarm/test_launch_check.py tests/test_size_limits.py -q -n 2 --cov=scripts.swarm_v2.admission --cov-report=term-missing
validation.output: admission, suite speed, tick and launch check tests 264 passed after the mutation fixes; admission 143 statements, 100 percent coverage
validation.lint: ruff check passed on changed Python files
validation.format: ruff format check passed on changed Python files
validation.limits: Only the allowlisted parameter count of _spawn (8) exceeds a limit, unchanged; complexity and branches within 12
validation.mutation: First CI run 37898294535: 20 survivors (4 tick, 16 admission); each killed by a new test or removed by restructuring an equivalent literal; next CI run qualifies

rollback_rehearsal.action: Set the global or swarm pending cap to zero: every new task is deferred with the reason distributed admission is set to zero, while a held reservation still activates so current attempts drain.
rollback_rehearsal.authoritative_objects: The per swarm pending reservation hash and the global pending sorted set; the outcome counter is observational.
rollback_rehearsal.proof: Case C admits with a zero cap policy over the same store, admits nothing and activates the held reservation; case C also restarts the admission owner mid hold and replays the same three reservations without a new admission. Admission state lives only in Redis and each step is one WATCH MULTI transaction, so the restart is a second admission owner over the same store; no mid transaction interruption point exists to exercise.

remaining_limitations: No Kubernetes runtime adapter exists yet to carry a PendingAdmission and create the pending Pods, so the tick path is inert in production; that adapter belongs to later packages and must construct Policy from its GitOps configuration, where the rollback is setting either cap to zero.
Ledger tasks have no resources field yet, so production tasks take the default request profile; the impossible request path is reachable only once a task carries resources.
Provider slots come from an injected source; the production source over account capacity is wired with the Kubernetes runtime.
pending_execution_admission_total is a per swarm Redis hash read through a method; no telemetry exporter emits it yet.
An exception raised between a claim and the spawn try block leaves the reservation held until it expires, as the claim itself is held today.
Mutation qualification of the fixes is pending the next CI run.
